items.title: The claude.ai Project instructions
items.why: A new claude.ai chat knows nothing; Project instructions and a handoff note in its knowledge carry your work across chats.

items.title: Context habits
items.why: Long threads get heavy and forgetful; a fresh session per day or task, and bulk reading in subagents, keep each one light.

items.title: The front-door instruction file
items.why: Without one file every session reads first, each session guesses who you are, what the rules are and what to load.

items.title: The git hook templates
items.why: Once committed, a leak stays in history; these refuse a secret, a conflict marker or a private address before the commit lands.

items.title: One git identity per folder
items.why: Company work committed under a personal address, or the reverse, is hard to undo; each folder picks its own address.

items.title: The grant ledger for risky acts
items.why: One recorded yes per force-push, merge, tag or hook skip, so a vague "clean up" never covers an act you did not name.
items.tokensNote: The rule line its card writes into the front door, at the standard size; bytes / 4, measured 2026-11-02.

items.title: MCP servers with the least access
items.why: Whatever a connected server can read, a session can read; recommended as soon as you have or want one.

items.title: The memory folder with its index
items.why: Chat history is not memory; one fact per file and a one-line index let the next session find what was learned.

items.title: The periodic rules audit
items.why: Rules drift from what enforces them; a read-only session every few months finds contradictions and gaps.

items.title: Signed commits
items.why: A signature proves a commit came from you; some companies require it, and a server shows signed commits as verified.

items.title: The memory vault
items.why: Shortening memory to make room loses it; the vault keeps the full text word for word and leaves a pointer behind.

items.title: One worktree per parallel session
items.why: Two sessions in one checkout switch branches under each other; a worktree each keeps their work apart.

items.title: USER.md: who you are
items.why: Every session guesses who you are and what you know; a short page you wrote ends the guessing.

items.title: RELATIONSHIP.md: what needs your OK
items.why: Without a written contract Claude asks about the obvious and skips the risky; the yes-list and the never-list settle it.

items.title: STYLE.md: how to write for you
items.why: Corrections to tone and format vanish by the next morning; recommended when output habits already annoy you.

items.title: SOUL.md: the values Claude works by
items.why: For those who want stated values, such as measure before claiming; most setups do without it.

items.title: A check before a session ends
items.why: Work left uncommitted or unpushed at the end of a session is found days later, or never; this names it before you stop.

items.title: A status line at the start of a session
items.why: Unpushed work, stale branches and an outdated front door show up at the start, in at most ten lines.

items.title: A decision log
items.why: A decision whose reason was never written gets argued again months later; one dated entry per decision keeps the why.
items.tokensNote: The rule line its card writes into the front door, at the standard size; bytes / 4, measured 2026-11-02.

items.title: Rules loaded only when needed
items.why: Every rule in the front door costs tokens on every turn; a short table says which file to read before which task.
items.tokensNote: A four-row table measured at 356 bytes, bytes / 4; the card gives light 63 and full 114.

items.title: One local check before every push
items.why: A push that breaks the build is found by someone else; one script that runs every test and lint first finds it on your machine.
items.tokensNote: The rule line its card writes into the front door, at the standard size; bytes / 4, measured 2026-11-02.

items.title: Check my setup
items.why: Adopted items drift: a hook switched off, a tool uninstalled; one command re-runs every check from your adoption plan.

items.title: Long jobs in named containers
items.why: A long job in a background shell dies unseen; a named container survives, can be watched, and keeps heavy work off your main machine.
items.tokensNote: The rule line its card writes into the front door, at the standard size; bytes / 4, measured 2026-11-02.

items.title: Merge commits only
items.why: A squash folds a branch into one commit and a rebase rewrites every one; a merge commit keeps the full history.
items.tokensNote: The rule line its card writes into the front door, at the standard size; bytes / 4, measured 2026-11-02.

items.title: A never-share list
items.why: Client names and internal terms leak through commits and posts; a private list the pre-commit checks refuses them first.
items.tokensNote: The rule line its card writes into the front door, at the standard size; bytes / 4, measured 2026-11-02.

items.title: A project registry
items.why: With more than three repositories a session loses track of what exists where; one index row each says where to start.

items.title: Commit messages and PR bodies that say why
items.why: A message that repeats the diff tells nobody why; a PR body that names what was verified and what was left undone does.
items.tokensNote: The rule line its card writes into the front door, at the standard size; bytes / 4, measured 2026-11-02.

items.title: Success criteria before the run
items.why: Criteria chosen after the results always fit them; writing them first is what lets a run fail.
items.tokensNote: The rule line its card writes into the front door, at the standard size; bytes / 4, measured 2026-11-02.

items.title: A sealed holdout
items.why: Every look at test data while tuning leaks it into the model; a holdout opened once, at the end, tells the truth.
items.tokensNote: The rule line its card writes into the front door, at the standard size; bytes / 4, measured 2026-11-02.

items.title: A baseline before any claim
items.why: A number with nothing to compare against proves nothing; a passing check can be a broken one.
items.tokensNote: The rule line its card writes into the front door, at the standard size; bytes / 4, measured 2026-11-02.

items.title: A small real-data seed
items.why: A pipeline tested only on made-up data breaks on the first real file; a small real slice, inside your data rules, finds that first.
items.tokensNote: The rule line its card writes into the front door, at the standard size; bytes / 4, measured 2026-11-02.

items.title: Negative results recorded as results
items.why: A failed idea that is not written down gets tried again; a recorded "no" saves the next run and keeps the record honest.
items.tokensNote: The rule line its card writes into the front door, at the standard size; bytes / 4, measured 2026-11-02.

items.title: The coding guidelines
items.why: Agents overbuild, guess silently and change more than asked; four short rules keep code simple and changes surgical.
items.tokensNote: Measured 2026-11-02: the guidelines text (2,340 bytes) plus its source line and a which-wins line, 2,523 bytes, bytes / 4; the card gives light 131 and standard 418.
